corrected_full_triples_personally_reread.rationale: Both address His servants and the sons of Jacob as His chosen ones. The psalm calls the offspring Abraham's, whereas Chronicles calls them Israel's. The corresponding address is retained without silently replacing either ancestral name.

corrected_full_triples_personally_reread.rationale: The psalm petitions God to remember the speakers with the favor of His people and to visit them with His salvation. Zechariah blesses God for having visited and accomplished redemption for His people. The shared divine visitation connects the communal petition with reported accomplishment, while the descriptions of the recipients remain distinct.

corrected_full_triples_personally_reread.relationship: Forgetting divine works within Israel's history
corrected_full_triples_personally_reread.rationale: Psalm 105 says the people hurried and forgot God's works and did not wait for His counsel. Psalm 77 recounts forgetting His benefits and the wonders He showed them. Both historical recitals identify forgetting divine acts, without importing the timing or counsel clause into the target.

Both name Moses and Aaron as targets of opposition. The psalm calls Aaron the Lord's holy one; Numbers quotes the challengers calling the whole congregation holy. These different attributions of holiness are preserved.

The psalm speaks of casting offspring among nations and scattering them through countries. In Ezekiel, God recounts His wilderness address to the children and raising His hand to scatter them among nations and countries. The paired dispersion language and wilderness context are particular.

The psalm places many rescues alongside provocation in the people's counsel and humiliation in their lawless deeds. Judges describes rescue through judges and renewed corruption when a judge died. The recurring rescue-and-disobedience pattern is particular; the explicit timing after a judge's death belongs to Judges.
